turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm mainly here because the health clinic for my logistics job wouldn't clear me to work. They told me my weight was too low. 

I don't really see it, honestly. To me, I just look lean... like someone who's ready to put in a hard day's work and stay quick on his feet. But they told me I had to come see someone, so here I am.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient reports presenting to the clinic because an occupational health screening evaluated his weight as too low to clear him for work.

turns.doctor_question: Are you afraid of gaining weight?
turns.patient_response:
I don't know if afraid is the word I'd use, but... yeah, I definitely don't want to put on weight. 

Like, if I eat rice, or bread, or something greasy, I just can't stop thinking that it's going to sit on me right away. It just stays in my head. So I'll always check the scale, or I'll see how my work belt fits the next morning, just to make sure I didn't let myself go.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient reports an intense aversion and persistent preoccupation with putting on weight after eating certain foods, regularly checking the scale and belt fit as reassurance.

turns.doctor_question: Do you intentionally eat less to keep your weight down?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Most days, I just keep it to black coffee... maybe a boiled egg or a little tuna. That's really all I need. And if I’m not actually moving freight on a shift, I just tell myself I don’t need a real meal anyway. If I'm not doing the heavy lifting and burning it off, there's no reason to eat a big plate of food.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient confirms intentionally restricting intake to minimal food such as black coffee, a boiled egg, or tuna, actively avoiding full meals.

turns.doctor_question: Do you see yourself as overweight?
turns.patient_response: Well, I wouldn't say I see myself as overweight overall, but... when I look in the mirror, especially at my stomach and waist, I just see areas that need to be tighter. I feel like if I'm not smaller and lean-looking, then I'm just not the disciplined man I used to be out on the warehouse floor. It's like, if there's any softness there, it means I'm slipping.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient explicitly links his self-worth and sense of discipline to his body shape and waist tightness, reflecting an undue influence of body weight and shape on self-evaluation.

turns.doctor_question: When you look in the mirror, do you mainly feel distressed that you’re too fat, or that there’s something wrong with the shape or appearance of a specific body part?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure what you mean by something wrong with the shape. I don't think any part of me looks deformed or anything like that. It's really just the fat. I look at my midsection and just feel like I'm too fat, like there's too much flab there. That's what gets to me.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient confirms body image distress focused on perceived fat and flab around the midsection.
symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient explicitly denies believing any body part looks deformed or having concerns about the shape/appearance of specific body parts outside of weight/fat.

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe your current low weight is a serious health problem?
turns.patient_response: Not really, no. I mean, my sister and my regular doctor keep saying I'm in some kind of danger, but... I think they're just making it a bigger deal than it actually is. They don't really understand. I'm just keeping myself light, you know? Keeping sharp and ready for work. I don't see that as a serious health problem at all.

symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient explicitly dismisses medical concerns and denies that their low weight poses any serious health risk, stating that others are making it a bigger deal than it is.

turns.doctor_question: Have you lost a lot of weight from what you used to weigh?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure if I'd call it a lot. I mean... I've definitely dropped some pounds, but I don't really keep track of the exact numbers on a scale. I just know I'm lighter than I used to be. I wouldn't say it's some extreme amount or anything, just enough to get that extra weight off.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed your sex drive has gone down?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm 55, so it's not exactly like when I was in my twenties, but I wouldn't say it's dropped off recently or anything. It just hasn't really been something I've paid much attention to, to be honest.

turns.doctor_question: What is your current weight and height?
turns.patient_response: I'm about 5 foot 10. As for my weight, I honestly couldn't tell you the exact number right now. Like I said, I don't really weigh myself or keep track of it like that. I just go by how my clothes fit and how I feel when I'm working.

turns.doctor_question: What is the lowest weight you’ve been at recently?
turns.patient_response: Well, like I was just saying, I really couldn't give you a number for that. I don't step on a scale, so I don't know what my lowest would be. I just know I'm smaller than I was based on my belt notches, but... yeah, I don't have an exact weight to give you.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any recent problems with erections?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't had any issues with that. Everything seems to be working fine on that front, I just haven't had any problems with it.

turns.doctor_question: What did the clinic tell you your weight was?
turns.patient_response: They just told me it was too low. That's actually why I'm here, honestly. The clinic for this logistics job I'm trying to get said my weight was too low to clear me for the physical. I don't really get it, to be honest with you. To me, I just look lean. I look like someone who's ready to work and, you know, stay quick on his feet. But yeah, they wouldn't clear me because they said it was too low.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient states that the clinic evaluated his weight as too low to clear him for a physical, confirming significantly low body weight.
symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient does not recognize the issue, dismissing the clinic's medical concern by stating he does not understand it and just considers himself lean and ready to work.

turns.doctor_question: Do you know what your weight was when the clinic measured it?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't. They didn't actually give me the exact number. The guy doing the physical just looked at the scale, told me I was under their minimum requirement, and said I needed to get checked out by a doctor before they'd clear me for the job. So... no, I really don't know what it was.

turns.doctor_question: Compared with your usual adult weight, have you lost a significant amount of weight?
turns.patient_response: No, I really haven't. I mean, my weight has pretty much always been around the same. I've always been on the leaner side, especially doing the kind of work I do. You're always moving, lifting, on your feet all day. So, no, I wouldn't say I've lost any significant amount of weight compared to what I usually weigh. I feel like I'm exactly where I normally am.

turns.doctor_question: About what did you usually weigh as an adult before you started eating this way?
turns.patient_response: I'm not exactly sure what you mean by "eating this way." I eat fine. But, uh, as for my usual weight... I don't really step on scales much. Like I said, I've just always been about this size. I couldn't give you an exact number from before, because it's just never been something I tracked. I just know my clothes fit the same as they always have.

turns.doctor_question: Before you started trying to eat less, did you used to wear larger clothes than you do now?
turns.patient_response: No, I've always worn the same size. Like I said, I'm not trying to eat less, and my weight hasn't really changed. I've been wearing the same work pants and shirts for years, and they all fit exactly how they always have.

symptom_reasoning.S026: The patient clearly states their weight has not really changed and their clothes have fit the same for years.
symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient explicitly states they are not trying to eat less.

turns.doctor_question: Has your current weight dropped a lot from what it used to be?
turns.patient_response: No, it hasn't. Like I was just saying, my weight hasn't dropped. I... I don't really know how else to put it, but no, I'm the exact same size I've always been.

turns.doctor_question: Has anyone who has seen your records told you that your weight used to be much higher than it is now?
turns.patient_response: No, nobody has ever said anything like that to me. I mean... if they looked at my medical records, they wouldn't see a higher weight anyway. My regular doctors haven't brought anything like that up because, like I've been saying, it just hasn't changed.

turns.doctor_question: Has your weight gone down a lot from what it used to be?
turns.patient_response: I feel like we're just going in circles here, Doc. No, it hasn't gone down at all. Like I've been saying, I haven't lost any weight. It's exactly the same as it's always been.

turns.doctor_question: Before the clinic physical, had any doctor ever told you that you were underweight?
turns.patient_response: No, never. No doctor has ever said anything like that to me. I've had regular checkups over the years, and... nobody's ever mentioned me being underweight. Everything has always been perfectly fine.
